question: The Indian Parliament comprises of the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**President and the two Houses**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian Parliament is a bicameral legislature consisting of the **President and the two Houses: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The President of India is an integral part of the Parliament, even though he/she is not a member of either House.
 
• **Lok Sabha** is the lower house of Parliament, also known as the House of the People.
 
• **Rajya Sabha** is the upper house of Parliament, also known as the Council of States.
 
• **Bicameral Legislature**
 
 
• It means the legislature is divided into two separate assemblies, chambers, or houses.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Sabha**

 
 
• Members are directly elected by the people of India.
 
• It has a maximum strength of 552 members.
 
• The tenure of Lok Sabha is 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha**
 
 
• Members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• It has a maximum strength of 250 members.
 
• It is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
 
 
• **President of India**
 
 
• The President is the head of the state and the supreme commander of the armed forces.
 
• The President has the power to summon and prorogue either House of Parliament and to dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
• The President's role in the legislative process includes giving assent to bills passed by Parliament, issuing ordinances, and ensuring the smooth functioning of Parliament.
